_doc: Focused suites iterate one style in depth; breadth runs one case of each style it names in `styles` and names every other catalog style in `not_covered` with the reason; a batch suite verifies one release's batch of changes: its gate cases run first and alone, and the rest run only if the gate passed (SPEC: E2E suites, Batch changes, then verify the batch). Every suite's `styles` is exactly the styles of its cases (test: SuiteTest.test_each_named_suite_selects_exactly_the_styles_its_claim_names).

not_covered.smoke: hello covers it in the smoke suite and as the batch gate; breadth is the generality gate for product styles
not_covered.parallel-graph: no parallel-graph case has a qualified passing baseline (SPEC Promotion: a style whose focused suite has never passed is not used to judge other changes); the four cases stay opt-in with --case
not_covered.hosted-platform: its cases deploy to a real hosted org (the Salesforce chess and Battleship cases need a developer org and the owner's explicit go for each deploy), so it cannot be a routine generality gate; it runs on its own with --case or its own suite
not_covered.brownfield: its cases, user-listing (build step 6, R10) and the ticket-assignment pair with its follow-on ticket-escalation (D7 of the brownfield-baseline design), have not run live, so the style has no qualified passing baseline (SPEC Promotion: a style whose focused suite has never passed is not used to judge other changes); they run with --case

covers.hello: cheap gate: new interfaces end to end (Improve completion, knowledge follow-up return, the driver)
covers.seat-reservations: stateful style; concurrency with the web chain (no shared /tmp names)
covers.battleship-scoring: follow-on: retention of spec, environment and architecture across runs
